1	# Framework: coding agents for DevSecOps at Papaya
2	
3	> Status: draft v3, for owner review · Updated: 2026-11-09
4	> Audience: a panel of Engineering and Compliance. Each layer ends with what it costs engineers and
5	> what it gives Compliance.
6	
7	## How to read this
8	
9	Eight layers. Each has a **Principle** (tool-independent), **On Papaya's stack** (Pulumi,
10	Serverless Framework, GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, k0s, Claude Code) and **Audit evidence** (records an
11	auditor can test without asking anyone). Copy-paste detail belongs in `examples/`.
12	
13	| Marker | Meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| 📖 R*x.y* | Documented. R*x.y* is a ✅/📖 row in `work/02-research.md` that quotes and links the official page. |
16	| ⚠️ R*x.y* | Inference, open question or "What this means for Papaya" conclusion in the research (sections 1.8, 2.9, 3.6, 3.7, 4.6, 5.6, 5.7, 6.5), or the ⚠️ part of a mixed row. Reasoned, not documented. |
17	| ⚠️ | Not verified at all, e.g. an illustrative command. |
18	| [design] | My proposal, built from documented parts, untested. Treat as ⚠️. |
19	
20	Nothing here was checked locally (✅): this is a design without access to Papaya's systems.
21	**GĐ-n** = assumption in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §4 (owner-confirmed: GĐ-1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11,
22	14; the others are marked "unconfirmed" where used); **S-n** = success criteria
23	(§5); **P/A-n** = problems (§1); **D1–D3** = owner decisions in research 6.6; **Options §n** =
24	`work/03-options.md`; **G-n** = gaps; **OD-n** = owner decisions on this draft (both at the end).
25	Earlier owner answers are cited with their source: "research 6.9.4 Q4", "framing Q8", "Options §9 Q2".
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 1. The decision in one page
30	
31	Engineering and Compliance disagree only about **writes to production**; reads of metadata and all
32	of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence (framing §3.1). Real customer data is layer 6.
33	
34	**Chosen approach "A + D2'"** (Options §9, owner decision 2026-11-09):
35	
36	1. **Default path:** every prod change is a pull request, approved by a named human who is not the
37	   author, applied by CI. Incidents included ("IaC first").
38	2. **Fallback (break-glass):** only when the PR path cannot be used, a human gets an approved grant
39	   with a 1-hour role session (effective window up to about 2 h, layer 7) and runs an approved command list in a terminal without an agent (layer 7) [design].
40	3. **Nothing standing:** no human or agent holds standing prod write; no long-lived credentials.
41	
42	| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
43	|---|---|
44	| A free loop in non-prod: read, change, deploy without approval (non-prod is synthetic or masked, GĐ-14; stores not yet scanned are excluded, layer 6). | Every prod change approved **before** apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent (limits below). |
45	| Read-only prod metadata for the agent. | No standing prod write (S1), no long-lived CI keys (S2, with an owner-approved exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials, kept as `production` environment secrets, OD1, OD6, layer 5). |
46	| Self-service PRs, one approval, same-day ship (S4). | One evidence chain per change; approval and change records ≥ 6 years (📖 R5.2.9; applied to change records ⚠️ R5.7 #2). |
47	| Incident lane: approval wait ≤ 15 min, 24/7 (S7). Decision-to-apply target ≤ 30 min (Options §9); current estimate 11–46 min ⚠️, measured first in rollout. | Agent-side controls as a second layer, not the control of record. |
48	
49	**Where the design falls short, stated openly:**
50	
51	- **The fallback meets the approval rule only partly** (approves a command list, not an applied
52	  change); accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2). It is a second, process-controlled path, while the
53	  framing asked for one technically enforced path (framing §3.3, Options §7). It stays narrow only
54	  if most incidents are expressible in IaC (unknown, Options §8); layer 7 measures this.
55	- **On GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply** (⚠️ R4.6 #1; Team assumed, GĐ-5).
56	  Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until an engineer approves the prod preview [design].
57	- **Admins can edit the gate**; logged, not prevented (logging 📖 R3.2.2; ability to edit ⚠️ R3.2.2,
58	  R3.6 #1). An admin's agent has
59	  the same power, because the agent uses its engineer's GitHub login (⚠️ R6.5 #10).
60	- **Some rules are process, not technology:** see "Process rules" in layer 1. The owner's rule
61	  "the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent" (OD5) is absolute as policy, but on
62	  laptops it is enforced by policy and training, not by a technical control: an agent could approve
63	  through its engineer's login, and no detection was found.
64	- **Incident approvers vs domain review:** for on-call engineers to approve any path at 2 a.m., they
65	  must be code owners of every deployable path, which weakens domain review on normal days. No
66	  verified solution yet (Options §1, §7, §8); S7 depends on it. Because on-call approvers only
67	  approve (OD7), a night incident needs two people awake: the incident responder and the on-call
68	  approver (the backup only replaces an unavailable primary).
69	- **One approver for high-risk changes.** L3 changes (IAM, stateful deletes, workflow files) get one
70	  approver, like L2, but that approver must own the path, and risky prod diffs stop for a look at
71	  the prod preview (OD2, layer 3). A single reviewer can miss things; this is the owner's trade-off
72	  for speed.
73	- **HIPAA applicability is a legal question** (⚠️ R1.11.1.11); the design treats Papaya as a
74	  business associate, as the brief implies.
75	
76	**Cross-cutting rules** (owner's balance principle, research 6.8):
77	
78	1. **The boundary is IAM and the CI gate.** Server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not
79	   a security boundary" (📖 R1.1.7); local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8).
80	2. **Assume prompt injection succeeds:** neither OWASP nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
81	3. **Friction where damage is large, none where it is small**, measured, with a time-boxed escape.
82	4. **Evidence by construction:** the path produces the records.
83	
84	### Roles
85	
86	| Role | Rule |
87	|---|---|
88	| Author (engineer + their agent) | Never approves own change; GitHub blocks PR authors from approving (📖 R3.3.1). |
89	| Approver | Always an engineer, never an agent (owner rule, OD5). Named in CODEOWNERS; ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (📖 R3.2.3); for an app-opened PR, ≠ the person who triggered it (⚠️ R3.3.4, layer 5). |
90	| Incident responder | Engineer who diagnoses and writes the fix or the JIT request. Never the on-call approver of the same shift (OD7). |
91	| On-call approver | Engineer on the on-call schedule, primary + backup, 24/7; wait ≤ 15 min (S7). While on call they only approve: they write no fix and file no JIT request, so the approver is always distinct from the author (OD7). The primary approves; the backup replaces an unavailable primary (OD2). No platform-team membership is required; all engineers follow one agreed approval procedure (OD2). |
92	| Data owner [design] | Named per tenant; co-approves real-data reads (layer 6). |
93	| Control owner | DevSecOps (1–2 people, GĐ-1); owns policies and metrics; not the only approver. |
94	
95	---
96	
97	## Layer 1 — Identity and access
98	
99	**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
100	written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
101	to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
102	
103	**On Papaya's stack**
104	
105	- **The engineer's access is the agent's access.** The agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and
106	  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse
107	  detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate
108	  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
109	  holds.
110	- **Process rules** that follow from this:
111	  - the JIT terminal runs no agent, though the grant is reachable from the same laptop (owner
112	    accepted as a process control, D2);
113	  - the incident-analysis session is meant to use only read-only roles (D2; `--restricted` per D3,
114	    research 6.9.4 Q2);
115	  - the real-data terminal runs no agent when the store holds PHI [design], same weakness as D2;
116	  - an agent never approves PRs: an owner rule (OD5), enforced on laptops by policy and training.
117	    GitHub blocks self-approval only. The auto-mode default block list
118	    excerpt read names "approving Claude's own pull request" (📖 R6.3.3); whether approving
119	    someone else's PR is blocked is unverified (⚠️), and the list
120	    applies only in auto mode. No detection was found (⚠️; `actor_is_agent` in the audit log has no
121	    documented meaning, R3.5.6).
122	- **IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1) [design names]:
123	  - `ProdReadMetadata`: metrics, redacted log groups, configuration; no data-plane read on claim
124	    stores; 1 h session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Until a service's logs are redacted at source
125	    (layer 6), it gets that service's metrics only. Lambda configuration can hold secrets resolved by
126	    Serverless in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7), so configuration reads are allowed per service only after
127	    its secrets move to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7). Cost: until then the agent reads
128	    timeout/memory from the IaC code;
129	  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad, non-prod accounts only;
130	  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7), via a partner product, the
131	    TEAM sample (📖 R2.4.1, R2.4.1b) or a small home-built flow (⚠️ R2.4.2) on the documented APIs
132	    `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2);
133	  - no standing prod-write permission set.
134	- **SCPs on the prod OU** [design] (SCPs cap member-account principals, 📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2):
135	  - deny data-plane reads on claim stores except application roles and the approved data-read role,
136	    by `aws:PrincipalArn` (📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Actions, e.g. `s3:GetObject`,
137	    `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, are incomplete and unchecked (⚠️ G13);
138	  - deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` / `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (⚠️ R4.6 #3) except
139	    CloudFormation `deploymentRole`s, the Pulumi prod deploy role (if Pulumi manages Lambdas) and the
140	    JIT roles. This closes `serverless deploy function`, which changes config outside CloudFormation
141	    (📖 R4.4.4), and needs `deploymentRole` set on every Serverless stack (📖 R4.4.5);
142	  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:userId` (📖 R2.4.4); protect the org trail (📖 R2.6.2).
143	  - Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters; no SCP applies to the management account
144	    (📖 R2.3.2, R2.3.4), so whatever deploys SCPs there is the most sensitive role (L3 path).
145	- **Sessions/MFA:** portal session length set on purpose; an IdP session can extend it silently
146	  (📖 R2.1.5, R2.1.6). MFA lives in the external IdP if one is used (📖 R2.1.7).
147	- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod role trusts only the `production`
148	  environment of the monorepo, in its `sub` format (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4; immutable format assumed,
149	  ⚠️ R3.7 A2), ideally customised with the deploy workflow's `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
150	- **CI → GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization, which Google
151	  requires (📖 R3.4.5b).
152	- **k0s, GCP and Firebase for humans:** same principles; mechanisms not researched (G1–G3). Today
153	  k0s is reached with kubeconfigs, no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim: no admin kubeconfig and no GCP
154	  owner role on laptops; prod deploys only from CI. Firebase is not on the GCP BAA list (📖 R5.5.3), so
155	  Firebase Hosting must hold no PHI (⚠️ R5.7 #7).
156	
157	**Audit evidence.** Identity Center assignment export (S1); CloudTrail `CreateAccountAssignment` /
158	`DeleteAccountAssignment` per grant (📖 R2.4.2), linked to its approval by request ID [design]; SCPs
159	and trust policies as Pulumi code; IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on policy PRs
160	(📖 R2.8.1); quarterly access review of permission sets and GitHub admins.
161	
162	**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write, keep fast prod reads and a free non-prod loop.
163	Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## Layer 2 — Agent runtime controls
168	
169	**Principle.** Agent-side controls are hygiene, not the boundary. They are central, versioned in git
170	and the same for everyone. Defaults are safe; overrides are measured. The session that reads
171	untrusted content holds as little power as possible (📖 R6.1.2).
172	
173	**On Papaya's stack**
174	
175	- **Delivery:** server-managed settings (available on Team, 📖 R1.1.5) for all laptops. With MDM, also
176	  an endpoint file; by default one managed source supplies most keys, so the two must carry the same
177	  keys or use `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` (📖 R1.1.3, R1.1.4). MDM is unknown; both are prepared.
178	- **Baseline** (template: Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json`, 📖 R5.5.4). All keys 📖 at the row cited:
179	
180	  | Key | Value and reason |
181	  |---|---|
182	  | `permissions.defaultMode` | `default` (Manual). A default, not a lock: users can switch to auto; VS Code remembers the last pick (D1, R6.9.3). |
183	  | `permissions.allow` | Read-only commands Papaya uses, to cut prompts (R6.9.3). |
184	  | `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` | `true`, one rule set (D1, research 6.9.4 Q4; R1.2.5). Cost: project and user rules are ignored, so the managed set must carry every deny/ask rule projects need; prompts likely rise (⚠️ research 6.9.4 Q4). |
185	  | `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` | `"disable"`: removes bypass mode (P3a; R1.2.2). Auto mode, where a classifier approves instead of a person, stays available (D1) and is measured through `permission_mode`. |
186	  | `permissions.deny` / `ask` | Deny credential paths (R5.5.4; `Read(...)` syntax ⚠️ R1.8 #5). Ask for `WebFetch`, which the sandbox domain list does not limit (R1.6.2); cost: a prompt per fetch. The HIPAA template denies WebFetch (R5.5.4); "ask" is a deliberate deviation so that documentation lookups still work. |
187	  | `requiredMinimumVersion` | ≥ 2.1.285 for `allowedProviders` (R1.1.15), which also covers `--restricted` (2.1.248, R6.9.1b) and the plugin-pin fix (2.1.179, R6.2.7); ≥ 2.1.295 if any managed hook uses `onFailure: "block"` (R1.5.2); and ≥ the latest fixed advisory at rollout (R6.3.9). It does not end running sessions and fails open on a bad value (R1.1.13). |
188	  | `allowedProviders` + `forceLoginOrgUUID` | `["anthropic"]` + Papaya's org; closes most bypasses on **endpoint-managed** machines (R1.1.15). `forceLoginOrgUUID` checks claude.ai sign-ins only, not Claude Console sign-ins (R5.5.5); with it set, sessions on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `apiKeyHelper` are refused (R1.11.3.11). |
189	  | `allowManagedHooksOnly` | `true` (R1.5.4). |
190	  | sandbox | `sandbox.enabled`, `failIfUnavailable`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`, narrow `network.allowedDomains` locked by `network.allowManagedDomainsOnly`; `credentials` / `filesystem.denyRead` on `~/.aws`, which the sandbox can otherwise read (R1.6.3, R1.6.4). |
191	  | MCP, plugins | Layer 4. |
192	  | OTel | Exporter on, content flags `0` (R1.1.20, R5.5.4). |
193	
194	- **Trade-off on AWS credentials [design].** With `~/.aws` hidden from the sandbox, the plan is to
195	  list `aws`, `pulumi` and `serverless` in `sandbox.excludedCommands`. Excluded commands run "with
196	  full access" (📖 R1.6.4), which likely includes the network (⚠️ inference). How the list matches
197	  commands (prefix or text, and chained commands) is not researched (⚠️). So these tools are an
198	  egress channel outside the allowlist, and an injected `aws` command could send out the SSO token
199	  cache itself. That token opens every role assigned to the engineer for the rest of the portal
200	  session (📖 R2.1.5, R2.2.2), including JIT or data-read grants added later in that session.
201	  Mitigations [design]: a short portal session (📖 R2.1.5); sign in again after a JIT or data-read
202	  grant is approved; an SCP that denies writes to resources outside Papaya's organization using
203	  `aws:ResourceOrgID` (key 📖 R2.3.8). Residual risk: token theft during a session. It is accepted
204	  because the engineer holds no **standing** prod write and no **standing** PHI read; during a JIT
205	  or data-read window the protection is the process rule in layer 1 (D2). Stronger option, phase 3:
206	  a separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions
207	  (⚠️ R6.5 #2).
208	- **Session types:**
209	
210	  | Session | Identity | Flags | Enforcement |
211	  |---|---|---|---|
212	  | Daily development (laptop) | non-prod roles + `ProdReadMetadata` | baseline | Auto mode by choice (D1); `--restricted` recommended (D3). |
213	  | Incident analysis (laptop) | meant to be `ProdReadMetadata` only | `--restricted --tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob"`, started in an empty scratch directory, not the repo [design] | Process rule (D3, research 6.9.4 Q1–Q2). No WebFetch, and file tools confined to the working directory (📖 R6.9.1b); Edit/Write are excluded only if `--tools` acts as an exclusive list (⚠️ unverified) (.1b), but Bash can still write in its working directory (📖 R1.6.3) and call any role in the cache. |
214	  | CI agent (hosted runner) | own GitHub App token; never `production` | `--restricted`, explicit `--tools`; all rules in a managed-settings file on the runner | Workflow file under CODEOWNERS (D3, research 6.9.4 Q5). The file is advisory if `Bash` is in `--tools` (layer 5). |
215	  | JIT terminal | JIT grant | no agent | Process rule (D2). |
216	  | Auto-mode environment (phase 3) | non-prod only | auto encouraged | D1 option (c). |
217	
218	- **Hard limits:** Bash rules are not a boundary (📖 R1.2.6); hooks fail open unless
219	  `"onFailure": "block"` (📖 R1.5.2); `--restricted` cannot be forced on laptops (📖 R6.9.1, R6.9.1c);
220	  on laptops **without MDM**, a different login, an API key or a `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` variable skips
221	  server-managed settings, `allowedProviders` included (📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ R1.8 #3, G11). So S5's
222	  "nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed" is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
223	- **Auto memory:** engineers review it and delete it after a suspicious session; residual risk with a
224	  named owner (D3).
225	- **Fallback:** switch to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers auto mode, a serious
226	  advisory appears, or an audit finds auto mode touched a protected scope (D1).
227	
228	**Audit evidence.** Managed settings in git with PR approvals; `/status` and `claude doctor` from
229	sampled machines (📖 R1.1.18); OTel `claude_code.tool_decision` (`permission_mode`) and
230	`claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user` (`duration_ms`, rubber-stamping signal) (fields 📖 research 6.6
231	D1 metrics; thresholds ⚠️). Settings-change audit events on Team: unknown (⚠️ R1.1.12).
232	
233	**Cost / value.** More prompts than auto mode, partly offset by the read-only allowlist. Compliance
234	gets one organization policy with evidence instead of personal choices (P3c).
235	
236	---
237	
238	## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
239	
240	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
241	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
242	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every change has exactly two people: one
243	who makes it and one who approves it (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of
244	that path) and adds an automatic stop on risky prod diffs, not more approvers. Incidents use the same
245	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
246	
247	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
248	|---|---|---|---|---|
249	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
250	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
251	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
252	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner of the L3 path ≠ author (in incidents: the on-call approver, if listed as owner) | same path, plus the risk stop |
253	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b) | layer 7 |
254	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | data owner + approver ≠ requester, with an agreement (GĐ-9) | layer 6 |
255	
256	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
257	the whole team (OD3). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need an approval
258	from the owners of those files rather than any code owner.
259	
260	**On Papaya's stack**
261	
262	- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
263	  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
264	  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
265	  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
266	  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
267	- **L3 approvals [design]:** a path-based rule requires 1 approval from the team that owns each L3
268	  path (📖 R3.2.4); GitHub stops the author from approving (📖 R3.3.1). The on-call schedule must
269	  include members of those teams, or the L3 owner teams must include the on-call engineers, so a
270	  night-time L3 fix can be approved. A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5) adds what
271	  the rules cannot: for app-opened PRs it excludes the person who triggered the agent, and it counts
272	  only human approvals, since an app's approval might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3).
273	- **Risk stop [design]:** the deploy job previews prod; on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change or
274	  an advisory policy finding it stops. A second PR adds `deploy-approvals/<sha>.yaml` with the
275	  preview hash, approved by an engineer ≠ author (it may be the same approver, who now sees the
276	  prod diff); the job continues only if the hash matches (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). A
277	  `mandatory` policy violation always blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2): the fix is a code change, or a
278	  change to the policy pack through its own L3 PR. Preview output is filtered for
279	  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
280	- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
281	  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
282	  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
283	  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4).
284	- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
285	  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
286	  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
287	  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
288	  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
289	- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
290	  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
291	  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
292	  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
293	- **State:** writable by deploy roles (and possibly the drift role, layer 7); Pulumi
294	  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
295	- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
296	  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1).
297	- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
298	  slow unrelated tests skipped [design].
299	
300	**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)
301	
302	The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
303	unavailable).
304	
305	1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
306	   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
307	2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
308	   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
309	3. R reviews the diff, and can catch a missing queue change, then approves.
310	4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
311	5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.
312	
313	**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks); run log and preview artifact, exported because
314	retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.
315	
316	**Cost / value.** One approval for every prod change (from the path owners for risky ones), none
317	in non-prod.
318	Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

359	## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening
360	
361	**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
362	least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
363	checks as human code (S10).
364	
365	**On Papaya's stack**
366	
367	- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
368	  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
369	  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
370	  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
371	  deploys may need a stored credential in GitHub: a kubeconfig or token for k0s, a Firebase token or
372	  service-account key for Firebase Hosting. The owner accepts this as an exception to S2 = 0 until it
373	  is checked whether k0s and Firebase deploys can use OIDC (OD1, OD6). Conditions [design]:
374	  - stored only as an **environment secret of `production`**, never as a repository secret. Anyone
375	    with write access can read repository secrets (📖 R3.5.3b), which would turn the exception into
376	    standing prod write for every engineer and their agent. Environment secrets and a deployment
377	    branch rule limited to `main` are available on Team for private repos (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3), and
378	    only the reviewed deploy workflow references the environment (layer 3);
379	  - that environment secret is the single source of truth: no copy elsewhere (OD1);
380	  - an owner, an expiry and rotation in the exception register.
381	  Residual risk: admins can change the environment, and a deleted environment comes back without
382	  protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); the alerts and settings comparison in layer 7 cover this. The exception
383	  covers **CI deploy credentials only**. Runtime credentials, such as a k0s autoscaler's AWS access to
384	  add or remove nodes, live in the cluster, not in GitHub; they follow layer 1 (no static keys, a
385	  role attached to the machine; ⚠️ not researched for k0s, G1).
386	- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
387	  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).
388	- **Pinning:** workflow lockfile (`gh actions-lock`) or full SHA, enforced by the org policy "Require
389	  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA"; the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so
390	  the deploy workflow lives in the same repo (📖 R3.5.5).
391	- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,
392	  `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc` (📖 R3.2.8; list ⚠️ R6.5 #5); CI validates the file, because
393	  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7).
394	- **No privileged triggers with untrusted code** (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` + checkout,
395	  📖 R3.5.4).
396	- **Agents in CI:** `claude-code-action` with a custom GitHub App limited to Contents, Issues, Pull
397	  requests (📖 R1.7.8); Anthropic workload identity federation, not a personal OAuth token (📖 R1.7.6);
398	  `--restricted` and explicit `--tools` (D3; passing it through `claude_args` unverified, ⚠️ research
399	  6.9.4 Q5); a managed-settings file on the runner, which also guards against mods (📖 R1.5.6; for
400	  federation auth ⚠️); MCP set fixed by CI because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
401	  (📖 R1.3.5); never `environment: production` (⚠️ R3.6 #4). Hosted runners give `sudo` (📖 R3.5.1),
402	  so with `Bash` in `--tools` the runner file is advisory (⚠️ R3.5.1, R3.6 #4).

405	  might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3; 📖 R3.2.5).
406	- **Required checks (S10):** secret scanning, dependency check, SAST (products: G4); IAM Access

418	## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence
419	
420	**Principle.** The design keeps PHI from reaching the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9).
421	Some paths rely on process (below), so this is a target, not a guarantee. Other customer
422	personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
423	by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved, name one
424	tenant, are time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
425	from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic or masked (GĐ-14).
426	
427	**On Papaya's stack**
428	
429	- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
430	  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` from phase 1 and the SCP from phase 2
431	    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
432	    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
433	  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
434	  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
435	    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
436	  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
437	- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
438	  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
439	  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
440	  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent (process rule, layer 1); the agent gets a
441	    redacted summary. This
442	    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
443	    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
444	  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9). Claim
445	    tables mix health, ID and bank data (research 1.11.4 L2), so a store that holds PHI is treated as
446	    PHI unless the agent reads a view or extract without PHI [design].
447	- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
448	  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
449	  1.11.4 L6).
450	- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default; the auto-mode
451	  classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions and 5.7 % of 1,000 synthetic exfiltration
452	  attempts (📖 R6.3.5). Broad allowed domains such as `github.com` are a documented exfiltration path
453	  (📖 R6.3.7). The incident session has no WebFetch, likely no edit tools (layer 2), and runs outside
454	  the repo, but its Bash can still write locally and send data out through excluded
455	  commands (layer 2), including the SSO token cache; "no standing write, no PHI read" limits what
456	  the token opens, except during a JIT or data-read window (layer 2 mitigations). Shared knowledge
457	  goes in `CLAUDE.md` under review; auto memory is unprotected unless `--restricted` (📖 R6.3.11, D3).
458	- **Tenants:** one tenant per data-read grant; a session that read one tenant's data does not post to
459	  shared places without review (⚠️ R6.5 #8, process). Logical separation in shared accounts is assumed
460	  (GĐ-3, unconfirmed).
461	- **Non-prod:** no prod copies (S11). A scan of non-prod stores runs at the start of phase 1 (tool:
462	  G4); a store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule (GĐ-14). Cost: until scanned, that store is
463	  not part of the free loop.
464	- **Local stores:** transcripts and memory hold what the agent read (research 1.11.4); set
465	  `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 in the HIPAA sample, 📖 R5.5.4; what it deletes ⚠️).
466	- **Cross-border (Vietnam example):** processing data collected in Vietnam on a platform abroad is a
467	  transfer (📖 R5.4.5); agent flows, including employee names in logs and transcripts, update the
468	  transfer impact assessment (⚠️ R5.7 #4, needs Papaya legal).
469	
470	**Audit evidence.** SCP/IAM text as the written access rule for sensitive data (📖 R5.4.3; ⚠️ R5.7 #5);
471	data-read requests and the data-read role's CloudTrail; planted-injection reports (layer 8); non-prod
472	scan results (S11).
473	
474	**Cost / value.** Debugging with redacted and synthetic data; a request for the rare real-data read.
475	Compliance gets "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores and by process
476	elsewhere, and a record per exception (S9).

480	## Layer 7 — Observability, audit, incident response and break-glass
481	
482	**Principle.** One tamper-evident evidence chain per prod change. One routed alert channel with a
483	named on-call, approvers included. Unapproved change is detected (drift, reconciliation). Break-glass
484	is approved before use, time-boxed and reconciled after.
485	
486	**On Papaya's stack**
487	
488	- **Audit stores:**
489	  - organization CloudTrail to a log-archive account with integrity validation (📖 R2.6.2, R2.6.4,
490	    R2.6.5); change records ≥ 6 years; raw-log retention for Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2).
491	    Data events only on PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS (cost 📖 R2.6.3; selection
492	    ⚠️ R2.9 #5), which makes the archive
493	    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);
494	  - GitHub org audit log kept 180 days, so exported (📖 R3.5.6);
495	  - alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`, `environment.update_protection_rule`,
496	    `environment.remove_protection_rule`, `environment.delete`, `protected_branch.policy_override`
497	    (📖 R3.5.6, R3.1.4; selection ⚠️ R3.6 #1). UI changes to the branch policy may leave no event, and a
498	    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
499	    with an expected copy (G8);
500	  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
501	    lost-record events (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️), stream treated as PHI (⚠️ R2.7.3);
502	  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2).
503	- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
504	  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
505	  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
506	  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).
507	- **Drift [design]:** its own role, trusted only from a `drift` environment on `main`; it can read
508	  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
509	  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2). On a DIY S3
510	  backend, preview needs state-write permission (📖 R4.3.3); whether a refresh preview writes more
511	  than locks is open (⚠️ R4.6 #2, G14). So either the drift role gets state write (and the same
512	  trust care as the deploy role), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection is used (📖 R4.3.2, Pro+). The
513	  latter runs on Pulumi Deployments, which holds credentials to prod, so it re-opens a side path that
514	  layer 5 excludes and needs the same trust narrowing and audit (📖 R4.4.9; ⚠️ R4.6 #6). CloudFormation
515	  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
516	  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
517	- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers only the named approver schedule (primary + backup engineers, 24/7),
518	  as decided in framing round 1. The primary approves; the backup steps in only if the primary is
519	  unavailable (OD2). On-call approvers only approve during their shift; the fix is written by an
520	  incident responder (OD7). Alert routing and the
521	  rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5).
522	- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:
523	
524	  | Step | Rule |
525	  |---|---|
526	  | When | The PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. |
527	  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
528	  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant (OD2). |
529	  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`; role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3), so the real window can approach 2 h; ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which must keep the user blocked for at least 12 h (📖 R2.4.4). |
530	  | Execution | The grant goes to the requester (the incident responder), who types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). D2 said the on-call person runs them; OD7 moves that to the responder, since on-call engineers only approve. |
531	  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
532	  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |
533	
534	  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage. Run
535	  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
536	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
537	
538	  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
539	  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
540	  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %, a value new in
541	  this draft). On a breach,
542	  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
543	- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
544	  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
545	  (D2, ⚠️).
546	
547	**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail; exported GitHub audit log; change records and monthly
548	reconciliation (S3, S8 ≤ 30 min); JIT requests, reconciliations, codify PRs; drift tickets; on-call
549	schedule and approval waits (S7).
550	
551	**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
552	Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
553	incidents, plus detection.
554	
555	---
556	
557	## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout
558	
559	**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
560	PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
561	attacks.
562	
563	**On Papaya's stack**
564	
565	- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); a platform team or named
566	  engineers (deploy workflows, rulesets, pipelines; whether Papaya has a platform team is unknown ⚠️); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
567	  Applicability); engineering leads (CODEOWNERS); engineering management (on-call schedule).
568	- **Policy as code:** managed settings, catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are
569	  files under CODEOWNERS; GitHub settings that are not files are compared with an expected copy
570	  (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8). Few GitHub admins, reviewed quarterly.
571	- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
572	  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (OD1; layer 2).
573	- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed). Framing Q8 (round 1): (1) remove long-lived CI credentials,
574	  (2) narrow standing prod access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2).
575	
576	  | Phase | Days | Items, in order |
577	  |---|---|---|
578	  | 1 | 0–30 | Measure the incident PR lane on one service (first task, Options §9). Non-prod data scan. OIDC for deploy workflows; remove long-lived keys (except k0s/Firebase under OD1); move laptop deploys to CI (GĐ-10, unconfirmed). Rulesets, CODEOWNERS and its validation check; required S10 checks. `ProdReadMetadata`; start moving secrets to runtime resolution and redacting logs at source, service by service. On-call approver schedule and a minimal incident-responder schedule (named, 24/7), because on-call approvers only approve (OD7); minimal JIT fallback **with** per-grant CloudTrail comparison and a drift check of the stacks it touched (by hand until automated, as D2 requires); risk stop in the deploy job (the policy-finding trigger works from phase 2); k0s/Firebase deploy credentials moved to `production` environment secrets; **then** remove standing prod write. MCP/plugin catalogue v1. Managed settings, phase-1 subset: `defaultMode` and `disableBypassPermissionsMode` (D1 said "immediately"), the keys that enforce the catalogue (`strictKnownMarketplaces`, `blockedMarketplaces`, `disableSideloadFlags`, `allowedMcpServers` + `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`, `disableClaudeAiConnectors`) and `requiredMinimumVersion` (needed by the plugin-pin fix). Also the read-only `permissions.allow` list, kept with Manual mode as D1 paired them (OD7b). |
579	  | 2 | 30–60 | Rest of the managed baseline and verification of the SSM option (moved here by the owner, OD4). SCPs: data-plane deny, Lambda update deny, revocation Deny, protection of the org trail, outside-org write deny; scheduled drift detection; automated JIT reconciliation; audit-log export, change records, monthly reconciliation; Access Analyzer and policy-pack checks; Aurora activity streams; emergency federation for Identity Center outages; alert routing and the rest of on-call. |
580	  | 3 | 60–90 | Planted-injection test on the real configuration (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.5; ⚠️ R6.5 #12); auto-mode non-prod environment (D1 c); separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions; first ISO evidence pack; 90-day review of D1–D3. |
581	
582	- **Exceptions:** a ticket with owner, reason and expiry.
583	- **Standards mapping** (⚠️ R5.6; HIPAA and Vietnam text 📖 R5.2, R5.4; ISO IDs recalled, not read,
584	  ⚠️ R5.1):
585	
586	  | Layers | ISO 27001:2022 Annex A (⚠️) | HIPAA Security Rule | Vietnam example |
587	  |---|---|---|---|
588	  | 1, 6 access | 5.15–5.18, 8.2, 8.3, 8.5 | 164.312(a)(2)(i); 164.308(a)(3)–(4) | Decree 356 Art. 4(2) |
589	  | 3, 5 change | 8.32, 8.31, 8.25, 5.3 | 164.312(c); 164.316(b) | — |
590	  | 7 logging, break-glass | 8.15, 8.16, 5.28 | 164.312(b); 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D); 164.312(a)(2)(ii) (mapping ⚠️ R5.7 #3) | Law 91 Art. 23 72 h notice (📖 R5.4.6; mapping new in this draft) |
591	  | 4 suppliers | 5.19–5.23 | 164.308(b), 164.314(a) | Law 91 Art. 20 |
592	
593	  "A named human approves" is Papaya's chosen way to meet these controls, not a literal requirement
594	  (⚠️ R5.7 #1).
595	- **Out of scope:** security of the production AI agents (A7a); noted as a follow-up.
596	
597	**Audit evidence.** Git history of policy files; monthly metrics; 90-day review minutes; exception
598	register; planted-injection reports.
599	
600	**Cost / value.** Steady, small overhead for DevSecOps and the platform team. Compliance gets a managed system
601	with owners and review dates.
602	
603	---
604	
605	## Gaps (not covered, or only as an open item, in `work/02-research.md`)
606	
607	| # | Gap | Layers |
608	|---|---|---|
609	| G1 | k0s: authentication, RBAC, audit logging, kubeconfig issuance (GĐ-4) | 1, 3, 6 |
610	| G2 | Firebase Hosting deploy from CI without a stored token | 1, 5 |
611	| G3 | Human and agent access to GCP (roles, data access) | 1, 6 |
612	| G4 | Secret scanning, dependency check, SAST, non-prod data scanning on the Team plan | 5, 6 |
613	| G5 | Paging and alert routing; approving a PR from a phone | 7 |
614	| G6 | SSM Automation `aws:approve` (read in `work/03-options.md` §2, not in 02-research) | 7 |
615	| G7 | GitHub Actions log and artifact retention, and export | 3, 7 |
616	| G8 | Rulesets and environment settings through the API | 7, 8 |
617	| G9 | How Linear and Slack MCP servers authenticate | 4, 6 |
618	| G10 | OIDC subject customisation (`job_workflow_ref`) on GitHub Team | 1 |
619	| G11 | Closing provider/login bypasses on laptops without MDM | 2 |
620	| G12 | `pulumi up` flag reference for the prod allowlist | 3 |
621	| G13 | IAM actions for every data-plane read (S3, SQS, Step Functions, Secrets Manager, RDS, ECS Exec, Lambda invoke) | 1, 6 |
622	| G14 | Which state writes a Pulumi refresh preview needs on a DIY S3 backend | 3, 7 |
623	
624	Open checks from `work/03-options.md` §8 remain open.
625	
626	## Owner decisions (2026-11-09)
627	
628	The owner answered the open questions of draft v3. English rendering; the original Vietnamese
629	answers are recorded in `work/session-log.md`.
630	
631	| # | Question | Decision |
632	|---|---|---|
633	| OD1 | Exception to S2 = 0 for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials? | Yes, provided each credential has a single source of truth. (The first reason given, continuous scale-in/scale-out, concerns runtime credentials; OD6 narrowed the scope.) |
634	| OD2 | L3: must one approver be from the platform team? | Not necessarily; one approval procedure is agreed for all engineers, and the on-call engineer is enough. Clarified in follow-ups: every change involves two people, one who makes it and one who approves; the on-call backup only replaces an unavailable primary. L3 needs one approver at all times, like L2. |
635	| OD3 | `CLAUDE.md` changes: L2 or L3? | L3, because the workflow must be consistent across the whole team. |
636	| OD4 | Move the rest of the managed baseline and the SSM check to phase 2? | Yes. |
637	| OD5 | "An agent does not approve PRs" only a process rule? | It is a rule: the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent. |
638	| OD6 | Scope of OD1: CI deploy credentials only, or also runtime scaling credentials? | CI deploy credentials (k0s kubeconfig/token, Firebase token in GitHub secrets) only, until it is checked whether k0s and Firebase can use OIDC. |
639	| OD7 | (a) If the on-call engineer writes an L3 fix, who approves? (b) Keep the read-only allowlist in phase 1? | (a) "While on call, never change the process"; clarified: on-call engineers only approve, and fixes are written by another engineer (the incident responder), so the approver is never the author. (b) Yes, as proposed. |

## 2026-11-08 — Session 2: git identity, transcripts, problem framing

- Git author: đặt `user.email` local cho repo, viết lại 2 commit chưa push sang email cá nhân;
  xoá `user.email` global theo yêu cầu người dùng. Tag `backup/pre-email-rewrite` giữ commit cũ (không push).
- Transcript commit nguyên bản; chấp nhận việc chứa email công việc của chính tác giả (ghi trong `CLAUDE.md`).

## 2026-11-09 — Thiết kế mục 1: `docs/framework.md`

- Viết `docs/framework.md` (8 tầng). Review độc lập 6 vòng; mỗi vòng có HIGH/MEDIUM mới (trích dẫn

  - OQ3 (`CLAUDE.md` L2 hay L3): "Xếp hạng L3, vì workflow cần thống nhất với cả team."

  - OQ5 (agent không duyệt PR): "là rule luôn, người duyệt PR luôn là engineer, không phải agent."
  - Không cần rút gọn file; cập nhật và chạy review vòng 7.
- Cách hiểu OQ2: L3 vẫn cần 2 engineer khác nhau, không cần thuộc platform; trong sự cố là on-call
  primary + backup. Owner xác nhận (nguyên văn): "Đúng vậy, vẫn là 2 engineer nhưng 1 primary và 1 backup."
- Review vòng 7: 3 HIGH, 8 MEDIUM, đã sửa. Câu hỏi mới OD6, OD7. Owner trả lời (nguyên văn):

  - Owner làm rõ lại OD2/OD7 (nguyên văn): "Mình hiểu nhầm ý này, ý của mình là chỉ cần 2 người, 1 người thực thi

content.content:
1	# Framework: coding agents for DevSecOps at Papaya
2	
3	> Status: draft v3, for owner review · Updated: 2026-11-09
4	> Audience: a panel of Engineering and Compliance. Each layer ends with what it costs engineers and
5	> what it gives Compliance.
6	
7	## How to read this
8	
9	Eight layers. Each has a **Principle** (tool-independent), **On Papaya's stack** (Pulumi,
10	Serverless Framework, GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, k0s, Claude Code) and **Audit evidence** (records an
11	auditor can test without asking anyone). Copy-paste detail belongs in `examples/`.
12	
13	| Marker | Meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| 📖 R*x.y* | Documented. R*x.y* is a ✅/📖 row in `work/02-research.md` that quotes and links the official page. |
16	| ⚠️ R*x.y* | Inference, open question or "What this means for Papaya" conclusion in the research (sections 1.8, 2.9, 3.6, 3.7, 4.6, 5.6, 5.7, 6.5), or the ⚠️ part of a mixed row. Reasoned, not documented. |
17	| ⚠️ | Not verified at all, e.g. an illustrative command. |
18	| [design] | My proposal, built from documented parts, untested. Treat as ⚠️. |
19	
20	Nothing here was checked locally (✅): this is a design without access to Papaya's systems.
21	**GĐ-n** = assumption in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §4 (owner-confirmed: GĐ-1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11,
22	14; the others are marked "unconfirmed" where used); **S-n** = success criteria
23	(§5); **P/A-n** = problems (§1); **D1–D3** = owner decisions in research 6.6; **Options §n** =
24	`work/03-options.md`; **G-n** = gaps; **OD-n** = owner decisions on this draft (both at the end).
25	Earlier owner answers are cited with their source: "research 6.9.4 Q4", "framing Q8", "Options §9 Q2".
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 1. The decision in one page
30	
31	Engineering and Compliance disagree only about **writes to production**; reads of metadata and all
32	of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence (framing §3.1). Real customer data is layer 6.
33	
34	**Chosen approach "A + D2'"** (Options §9, owner decision 2026-11-09):
35	
36	1. **Default path:** every prod change is a pull request, approved by a named human who is not the
37	   author, applied by CI. Incidents included ("IaC first").
38	2. **Fallback (break-glass):** only when the PR path cannot be used, a human gets an approved grant
39	   with a 1-hour role session (effective window up to about 2 h, layer 7) and runs an approved command list in a terminal without an agent (layer 7) [design].
40	3. **Nothing standing:** no human or agent holds standing prod write; no long-lived credentials.
41	
42	| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
43	|---|---|
44	| A free loop in non-prod: read, change, deploy without approval (non-prod is synthetic or masked, GĐ-14; stores not yet scanned are excluded, layer 6). | Every prod change approved **before** apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent (limits below). |
45	| Read-only prod metadata for the agent. | No standing prod write (S1), no long-lived CI keys (S2, with an owner-approved exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials, kept as `production` environment secrets, OD1, OD6, layer 5). |
46	| Self-service PRs, one approval, same-day ship (S4). | One evidence chain per change; approval and change records ≥ 6 years (📖 R5.2.9; applied to change records ⚠️ R5.7 #2). |
47	| Incident lane: approval wait ≤ 15 min, 24/7 (S7). Decision-to-apply target ≤ 30 min (Options §9); current estimate 11–46 min ⚠️, measured first in rollout. | Agent-side controls as a second layer, not the control of record. |
48	
49	**Where the design falls short, stated openly:**
50	
51	- **The fallback meets the approval rule only partly** (approves a command list, not an applied
52	  change); accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2). It is a second, process-controlled path, while the
53	  framing asked for one technically enforced path (framing §3.3, Options §7). It stays narrow only
54	  if most incidents are expressible in IaC (unknown, Options §8); layer 7 measures this.
55	- **On GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply** (⚠️ R4.6 #1; Team assumed, GĐ-5).
56	  Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until an engineer approves the prod preview [design].
57	- **Admins can edit the gate**; logged, not prevented (logging 📖 R3.2.2; ability to edit ⚠️ R3.2.2,
58	  R3.6 #1). An admin's agent has
59	  the same power, because the agent uses its engineer's GitHub login (⚠️ R6.5 #10).
60	- **Some rules are process, not technology:** see "Process rules" in layer 1. The owner's rule
61	  "the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent" (OD5) is absolute as policy, but on
62	  laptops it is enforced by policy and training, not by a technical control: an agent could approve
63	  through its engineer's login, and no detection was found.
64	- **Incident approvers vs domain review:** for on-call engineers to approve any path at 2 a.m., they
65	  must be code owners of every deployable path, which weakens domain review on normal days. No
66	  verified solution yet (Options §1, §7, §8); S7 depends on it. Because on-call approvers only
67	  approve (OD7), a night incident needs two people awake: the incident responder and the on-call
68	  approver (the backup only replaces an unavailable primary).
69	- **One approver for high-risk changes.** L3 changes (IAM, stateful deletes, workflow files) get one
70	  approver, like L2, but that approver must own the path, and risky prod diffs stop for a look at
71	  the prod preview (OD2, layer 3). A single reviewer can miss things; this is the owner's trade-off
72	  for speed.
73	- **HIPAA applicability is a legal question** (⚠️ R1.11.1.11); the design treats Papaya as a
74	  business associate, as the brief implies.
75	
76	**Cross-cutting rules** (owner's balance principle, research 6.8):
77	
78	1. **The boundary is IAM and the CI gate.** Server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not
79	   a security boundary" (📖 R1.1.7); local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8).
80	2. **Assume prompt injection succeeds:** neither OWASP nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
81	3. **Friction where damage is large, none where it is small**, measured, with a time-boxed escape.
82	4. **Evidence by construction:** the path produces the records.
83	
84	### Roles
85	
86	| Role | Rule |
87	|---|---|
88	| Author (engineer + their agent) | Never approves own change; GitHub blocks PR authors from approving (📖 R3.3.1). |
89	| Approver | Always an engineer, never an agent (owner rule, OD5). Named in CODEOWNERS; ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (📖 R3.2.3); for an app-opened PR, ≠ the person who triggered it (⚠️ R3.3.4, layer 5). |
90	| Incident responder | Engineer who diagnoses and writes the fix or the JIT request. Never the on-call approver of the same shift (OD7). |
91	| On-call approver | Engineer on the on-call schedule, primary + backup, 24/7; wait ≤ 15 min (S7). While on call they only approve: they write no fix and file no JIT request, so the approver is always distinct from the author (OD7). The primary approves; the backup replaces an unavailable primary (OD2). No platform-team membership is required; all engineers follow one agreed approval procedure (OD2). |
92	| Data owner [design] | Named per tenant; co-approves real-data reads (layer 6). |
93	| Control owner | DevSecOps (1–2 people, GĐ-1); owns policies and metrics; not the only approver. |

97	## Layer 1 — Identity and access
98	
99	**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
100	written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
101	to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
102	
103	**On Papaya's stack**
104	
105	- **The engineer's access is the agent's access.** The agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and
106	  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse
107	  detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate
108	  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
109	  holds.
110	- **Process rules** that follow from this:
111	  - the JIT terminal runs no agent, though the grant is reachable from the same laptop (owner
112	    accepted as a process control, D2);
113	  - the incident-analysis session is meant to use only read-only roles (D2; `--restricted` per D3,
114	    research 6.9.4 Q2);
115	  - the real-data terminal runs no agent when the store holds PHI [design], same weakness as D2;
116	  - an agent never approves PRs: an owner rule (OD5), enforced on laptops by policy and training.
117	    GitHub blocks self-approval only. The auto-mode default block list
118	    excerpt read names "approving Claude's own pull request" (📖 R6.3.3); whether approving
119	    someone else's PR is blocked is unverified (⚠️), and the list
120	    applies only in auto mode. No detection was found (⚠️; `actor_is_agent` in the audit log has no
121	    documented meaning, R3.5.6).
122	- **IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1) [design names]:
123	  - `ProdReadMetadata`: metrics, redacted log groups, configuration; no data-plane read on claim
124	    stores; 1 h session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Until a service's logs are redacted at source
125	    (layer 6), it gets that service's metrics only. Lambda configuration can hold secrets resolved by
126	    Serverless in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7), so configuration reads are allowed per service only after
127	    its secrets move to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7). Cost: until then the agent reads
128	    timeout/memory from the IaC code;
129	  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad, non-prod accounts only;
130	  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7), via a partner product, the
131	    TEAM sample (📖 R2.4.1, R2.4.1b) or a small home-built flow (⚠️ R2.4.2) on the documented APIs
132	    `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2);
133	  - no standing prod-write permission set.
134	- **SCPs on the prod OU** [design] (SCPs cap member-account principals, 📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2):
135	  - deny data-plane reads on claim stores except application roles and the approved data-read role,
136	    by `aws:PrincipalArn` (📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Actions, e.g. `s3:GetObject`,
137	    `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, are incomplete and unchecked (⚠️ G13);
138	  - deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` / `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (⚠️ R4.6 #3) except
139	    CloudFormation `deploymentRole`s, the Pulumi prod deploy role (if Pulumi manages Lambdas) and the
140	    JIT roles. This closes `serverless deploy function`, which changes config outside CloudFormation
141	    (📖 R4.4.4), and needs `deploymentRole` set on every Serverless stack (📖 R4.4.5);
142	  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:userId` (📖 R2.4.4); protect the org trail (📖 R2.6.2).
143	  - Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters; no SCP applies to the management account
144	    (📖 R2.3.2, R2.3.4), so whatever deploys SCPs there is the most sensitive role (L3 path).
145	- **Sessions/MFA:** portal session length set on purpose; an IdP session can extend it silently
146	  (📖 R2.1.5, R2.1.6). MFA lives in the external IdP if one is used (📖 R2.1.7).
147	- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod role trusts only the `production`
148	  environment of the monorepo, in its `sub` format (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4; immutable format assumed,
149	  ⚠️ R3.7 A2), ideally customised with the deploy workflow's `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
150	- **CI → GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization, which Google
151	  requires (📖 R3.4.5b).
152	- **k0s, GCP and Firebase for humans:** same principles; mechanisms not researched (G1–G3). Today
153	  k0s is reached with kubeconfigs, no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim: no admin kubeconfig and no GCP
154	  owner role on laptops; prod deploys only from CI. Firebase is not on the GCP BAA list (📖 R5.5.3), so
155	  Firebase Hosting must hold no PHI (⚠️ R5.7 #7).
156	
157	**Audit evidence.** Identity Center assignment export (S1); CloudTrail `CreateAccountAssignment` /
158	`DeleteAccountAssignment` per grant (📖 R2.4.2), linked to its approval by request ID [design]; SCPs
159	and trust policies as Pulumi code; IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on policy PRs
160	(📖 R2.8.1); quarterly access review of permission sets and GitHub admins.
161	
162	**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write, keep fast prod reads and a free non-prod loop.
163	Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced.

167	## Layer 2 — Agent runtime controls
168	
169	**Principle.** Agent-side controls are hygiene, not the boundary. They are central, versioned in git
170	and the same for everyone. Defaults are safe; overrides are measured. The session that reads
171	untrusted content holds as little power as possible (📖 R6.1.2).
172	
173	**On Papaya's stack**
174	
175	- **Delivery:** server-managed settings (available on Team, 📖 R1.1.5) for all laptops. With MDM, also
176	  an endpoint file; by default one managed source supplies most keys, so the two must carry the same
177	  keys or use `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` (📖 R1.1.3, R1.1.4). MDM is unknown; both are prepared.
178	- **Baseline** (template: Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json`, 📖 R5.5.4). All keys 📖 at the row cited:
179	
180	  | Key | Value and reason |
181	  |---|---|
182	  | `permissions.defaultMode` | `default` (Manual). A default, not a lock: users can switch to auto; VS Code remembers the last pick (D1, R6.9.3). |
183	  | `permissions.allow` | Read-only commands Papaya uses, to cut prompts (R6.9.3). |
184	  | `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` | `true`, one rule set (D1, research 6.9.4 Q4; R1.2.5). Cost: project and user rules are ignored, so the managed set must carry every deny/ask rule projects need; prompts likely rise (⚠️ research 6.9.4 Q4). |
185	  | `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` | `"disable"`: removes bypass mode (P3a; R1.2.2). Auto mode, where a classifier approves instead of a person, stays available (D1) and is measured through `permission_mode`. |
186	  | `permissions.deny` / `ask` | Deny credential paths (R5.5.4; `Read(...)` syntax ⚠️ R1.8 #5). Ask for `WebFetch`, which the sandbox domain list does not limit (R1.6.2); cost: a prompt per fetch. The HIPAA template denies WebFetch (R5.5.4); "ask" is a deliberate deviation so that documentation lookups still work. |
187	  | `requiredMinimumVersion` | ≥ 2.1.285 for `allowedProviders` (R1.1.15), which also covers `--restricted` (2.1.248, R6.9.1b) and the plugin-pin fix (2.1.179, R6.2.7); ≥ 2.1.295 if any managed hook uses `onFailure: "block"` (R1.5.2); and ≥ the latest fixed advisory at rollout (R6.3.9). It does not end running sessions and fails open on a bad value (R1.1.13). |
188	  | `allowedProviders` + `forceLoginOrgUUID` | `["anthropic"]` + Papaya's org; closes most bypasses on **endpoint-managed** machines (R1.1.15). `forceLoginOrgUUID` checks claude.ai sign-ins only, not Claude Console sign-ins (R5.5.5); with it set, sessions on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `apiKeyHelper` are refused (R1.11.3.11). |
189	  | `allowManagedHooksOnly` | `true` (R1.5.4). |
190	  | sandbox | `sandbox.enabled`, `failIfUnavailable`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`, narrow `network.allowedDomains` locked by `network.allowManagedDomainsOnly`; `credentials` / `filesystem.denyRead` on `~/.aws`, which the sandbox can otherwise read (R1.6.3, R1.6.4). |
191	  | MCP, plugins | Layer 4. |
192	  | OTel | Exporter on, content flags `0` (R1.1.20, R5.5.4). |
193	
194	- **Trade-off on AWS credentials [design].** With `~/.aws` hidden from the sandbox, the plan is to
195	  list `aws`, `pulumi` and `serverless` in `sandbox.excludedCommands`. Excluded commands run "with
196	  full access" (📖 R1.6.4), which likely includes the network (⚠️ inference). How the list matches
197	  commands (prefix or text, and chained commands) is not researched (⚠️). So these tools are an
198	  egress channel outside the allowlist, and an injected `aws` command could send out the SSO token
199	  cache itself. That token opens every role assigned to the engineer for the rest of the portal
200	  session (📖 R2.1.5, R2.2.2), including JIT or data-read grants added later in that session.
201	  Mitigations [design]: a short portal session (📖 R2.1.5); sign in again after a JIT or data-read
202	  grant is approved; an SCP that denies writes to resources outside Papaya's organization using
203	  `aws:ResourceOrgID` (key 📖 R2.3.8). Residual risk: token theft during a session. It is accepted
204	  because the engineer holds no **standing** prod write and no **standing** PHI read; during a JIT
205	  or data-read window the protection is the process rule in layer 1 (D2). Stronger option, phase 3:
206	  a separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions
207	  (⚠️ R6.5 #2).
208	- **Session types:**
209	
210	  | Session | Identity | Flags | Enforcement |
211	  |---|---|---|---|
212	  | Daily development (laptop) | non-prod roles + `ProdReadMetadata` | baseline | Auto mode by choice (D1); `--restricted` recommended (D3). |
213	  | Incident analysis (laptop) | meant to be `ProdReadMetadata` only | `--restricted --tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob"`, started in an empty scratch directory, not the repo [design] | Process rule (D3, research 6.9.4 Q1–Q2). No WebFetch, and file tools confined to the working directory (📖 R6.9.1b); Edit/Write are excluded only if `--tools` acts as an exclusive list (⚠️ unverified) (.1b), but Bash can still write in its working directory (📖 R1.6.3) and call any role in the cache. |
214	  | CI agent (hosted runner) | own GitHub App token; never `production` | `--restricted`, explicit `--tools`; all rules in a managed-settings file on the runner | Workflow file under CODEOWNERS (D3, research 6.9.4 Q5). The file is advisory if `Bash` is in `--tools` (layer 5). |
215	  | JIT terminal | JIT grant | no agent | Process rule (D2). |
216	  | Auto-mode environment (phase 3) | non-prod only | auto encouraged | D1 option (c). |
217

223	- **Auto memory:** engineers review it and delete it after a suspicious session; residual risk with a

225	- **Fallback:** switch to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers auto mode, a serious

238	## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
239	
240	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
241	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
242	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every change has exactly two people: one
243	who makes it and one who approves it (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of
244	that path) and adds an automatic stop on risky prod diffs, not more approvers. Incidents use the same
245	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
246	
247	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
248	|---|---|---|---|---|
249	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
250	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
251	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
252	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner of the L3 path ≠ author (in incidents: the on-call approver, if listed as owner) | same path, plus the risk stop |
253	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b) | layer 7 |
254	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | data owner + approver ≠ requester, with an agreement (GĐ-9) | layer 6 |
255	
256	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
257	the whole team (OD3). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need an approval
258	from the owners of those files rather than any code owner.
259	
260	**On Papaya's stack**
261	
262	- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
263	  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
264	  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
265	  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
266	  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
267	- **L3 approvals [design]:** a path-based rule requires 1 approval from the team that owns each L3
268	  path (📖 R3.2.4); GitHub stops the author from approving (📖 R3.3.1). The on-call schedule must
269	  include members of those teams, or the L3 owner teams must include the on-call engineers, so a
270	  night-time L3 fix can be approved. A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5) adds what
271	  the rules cannot: for app-opened PRs it excludes the person who triggered the agent, and it counts
272	  only human approvals, since an app's approval might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3).
273	- **Risk stop [design]:** the deploy job previews prod; on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change or
274	  an advisory policy finding it stops. A second PR adds `deploy-approvals/<sha>.yaml` with the
275	  preview hash, approved by an engineer ≠ author (it may be the same approver, who now sees the
276	  prod diff); the job continues only if the hash matches (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). A
277	  `mandatory` policy violation always blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2): the fix is a code change, or a
278	  change to the policy pack through its own L3 PR. Preview output is filtered for
279	  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
280	- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
281	  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
282	  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
283	  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4).
284	- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
285	  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
286	  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
287	  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
288	  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
289	- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
290	  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
291	  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
292	  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
293	- **State:** writable by deploy roles (and possibly the drift role, layer 7); Pulumi
294	  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
295	- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
296	  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1).
297	- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
298	  slow unrelated tests skipped [design].
299	
300	**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)
301	
302	The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
303	unavailable).
304	
305	1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
306	   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
307	2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
308	   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
309	3. R reviews the diff, and can catch a missing queue change, then approves.
310	4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
311	5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.
312	
313	**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks); run log and preview artifact, exported because
314	retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.
315	
316	**Cost / value.** One approval for every prod change (from the path owners for risky ones), none
317	in non-prod.
318	Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

322	## Layer 4 — Supply chain for MCP servers and plugins
323	
324	**Principle.** MCP servers, plugins and hooks run with the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5).
325	Only reviewed, pinned entries from a catalogue are allowed. The catalogue is the inventory (P4c).
326	Review takes ≤ 5 working days (S6), or people work around it.
327	
328	**On Papaya's stack**
329	
330	- **Plugins:** a private marketplace repo with `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (📖 R1.4.1), sources
331	  pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b, link only). Managed `strictKnownMarketplaces` = Papaya only,
332	  `blockedMarketplaces`, `enabledPlugins: false` to pull one (📖 R1.4.2), checked before download and
333	  at session start (📖 R1.4.3). `disableSideloadFlags` rejects `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`,
334	  `--agents`, `--mcp-config` but not `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add` (📖 R1.4.2). With
335	  `allowManagedHooksOnly`, plugin hooks run only for force-enabled plugins (📖 R1.5.4). User mods are
336	  blocked by the `allowManagedModsOnly` option under `pluginConfigs` → `cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin`
337	  → `options` (📖 R1.5.6). The version floor covers the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7).
338	- **MCP:** "approved catalogue" = `allowedMcpServers` + `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true`; without
339	  the lock users can widen it (📖 R1.3.1, R1.3.4). Match by `serverUrl` or `serverCommand`, never
340	  `serverName` ("not a security control", 📖 R1.3.3); the argv pins an exact version (⚠️ R6.4.4).
341	  `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` (📖 R1.3.7). With MDM, `managed-mcp.json` gives exclusive control;
342	  it cannot come from server-managed settings (📖 R1.3.2).
343	- **Review checklist** [design]: publisher; local `stdio` or remote (📖 R6.4.3); what it reads and where
344	  it sends data, with a supplier-register entry and BAA/DPA status (⚠️ R5.6); no token passthrough
345	  (📖 R6.4.2); write tools for Slack, Linear, GitHub only where needed (⚠️ R6.5 #6); pinned version,
346	  reviewer, date.
347	- **Known gaps:** no per-group targeting in server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.6, R1.4.4); tool
348	  description changes after approval are not covered (⚠️ research 6.6).
349	
350	**Audit evidence.** Catalogue file in git (each entry = an approved PR); supplier register; OTel
351	`claude_code.plugin_installed` / `plugin_loaded` (📖 R1.4.6). MCP tool logging needs
352	`OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` (📖 R1.3.8); it stays off until we know whether it logs tool inputs (⚠️).
353	
354	**Cost / value.** Up to 5 days' wait for a new tool. Compliance gets an asset inventory and supplier
355	records.

359	## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening
360	
361	**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
362	least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
363	checks as human code (S10).
364	
365	**On Papaya's stack**
366	
367	- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
368	  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
369	  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
